displayName: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location

tests.name: Execute a process from a directory masquerading as the current parent directory
tests.description: Create and execute a process from a directory masquerading as the current parent directory (`...` instead of normal `..`)

tests.name: Masquerade as a built-in system executable
tests.description: Launch an executable that attempts to masquerade as a legitimate executable.

tests.name: Masquerading cmd.exe as VEDetector.exe
tests.description:
This test simulates an adversary renaming cmd.exe to VEDetector.exe to masquerade as a legitimate application.
The test copies cmd.exe, renames it to VEDetector.exe, adds a registry run key for persistence, and executes the renamed binary.
This technique may be used to evade detection by mimicking legitimate software names or locations.

**Expected Output:**
- A new process named VEDetector.exe appears in the process list, but its behavior matches cmd.exe.
- SIEM/EDR systems may detect this as suspicious process activity (e.g., Sysmon Event ID 1 for process creation, or Event ID 13 for registry modifications).
- Registry modification in HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run may

tests.name: WMIC masquerade as ncv.exe in temp directory
tests.description:
Copies %SystemRoot%\System32\wbem\wmic.exe to a temporary directory,
renames it to ncv.exe, and executes it to retrieve OS version information.
This simulates an adversary using a renamed trusted binary from an
unexpected location to evade detection.
